title: Cancellation Notice: Days Given and Days Required for In-Person Appointments
content:
**Clause 1.** A patient cancellation of an In-Person Appointments visit is timely when the notice days it gives are at least the notice days the visit requires, and late otherwise.

**Clause 2.** The notice days given are the calendar days from the date of the cancellation to the scheduled date of the visit, the cancellation date not counted and the scheduled date counted.

**Clause 3.** The notice days required are the visit type's cancellation notice hours divided by 24 and rounded up to a whole day. Days by which the notice days required rise are added together onto that whole-day figure, and a reduction in the notice counted applies only to the notice days given.

### The rounded figure by notice hours

| Cancellation notice of the visit type | Divided by 24 | Rounded up to a whole day |
|---|---|---|
| 24 hours | 1 | 1 day |
| 48 hours | 2 | 2 days |
| 72 hours | 3 | 3 days |

A figure that does not divide evenly is rounded up: 30 hours, for instance, would give 1.25 and so 2 days.

### Counting the days given

The cancellation date itself is not counted and the scheduled date is. A cancellation made on the scheduled date gives 0 days; one made the day before gives 1 day.

### Worked figures (hypothetical inputs)

1. A Specialist Consultation is scheduled for 2026-11-20 and the patient cancels on 2026-11-18. Days given: 2. The visit type's notice is 48 hours, so the days required are 2. Since 2 is at least 2, the cancellation is **timely**.
2. The same visit, cancelled on 2026-11-19. Days given: 1, against 2 required, so the cancellation is **late**.
3. An In-Office Procedure Visit is scheduled for 2026-12-04 and cancelled on 2026-12-01. Days given: 3; days required: 72 hours divided by 24, that is 3. The cancellation is **timely**.

### Points of judgement

- Only whole calendar dates enter the count; the time of day of the cancellation and of the scheduled start does not change the days given.
- The comparison is "at least": days given equal to the days required make the cancellation timely.
